_comment: Everything the scanner needs to know about a warehouse. Derived from
warehouse/warehouse.yaml; the field-by-field mapping is in the README.
Nothing here is baked into scanner.py, so a new warehouse is a new file.
Coordinates are Gazebo world coordinates, metres. Yaw follows MAVSDK:
0 is north (+Y), positive is clockwise, so +90 faces +X and -90 faces -X.
A face is given by the x of the shelf surface itself, not by the aisle
centre line. Where the vehicle flies follows from face_x and standoff,
which lets it stand closer to the shelf than the middle of the aisle.
That matters here: the real C27 hires stream is 1024x768, and at the
1.216 m aisle centre a 2.8 mm module resolves to 2.04 px, below the 3 px
a QR needs. At 0.80 m it is 3.10 px.
_ground_offset_note: How far base_link, and therefore the camera, rests above the floor when
the vehicle is landed. Commanded altitudes are relative to the spawn
point, which is captured on the ground, so without this every commanded
height is this much too high in world terms. Measured by back-computing
the camera height from decoded labels of known position: +0.221, +0.232
and +0.227 m at the three shelf levels.
It cost 63 percent of a scan. Labels sat 0.16 to 0.26 m below the optical
axis instead of on it, so only the topmost of the three box heights fell
inside the 0.234 m half-frame; the other two read 22 and 0 percent.
